title: Clarifying question generation
description: When a request is genuinely ambiguous ('book a table' — where? when? how many?), the agent asks targeted clarifying questions instead of guessing. Good clarification asks the minimum questions that maximally reduce uncertainty, ordered by importance.
method: Detect ambiguity (multiple plausible parses); rank missing slots by information value; ask the top 1-2 as concise questions; proceed when resolved.
usage: Ask only what you need; never ask what you can infer from context; make questions easy to answer.

demo.code:
req = 'book a table'
missing = ['where', 'when', 'party size']
print(f'ambiguous: {req!r} -> ask: "Where, and for when?" (covers {missing[:2]})')

title: Ambiguity scoring and thresholds
description: Not every request needs clarification — the agent scores ambiguity (entropy over plausible parses) and only interrupts when it exceeds a threshold. Low ambiguity: act and note the assumption. High ambiguity: ask. The threshold is the product decision that balances friction against mistakes.
method: Score parses by probability; compute entropy; above threshold -> clarify; below -> act with stated assumption; log borderline cases.
usage: Tune the threshold on real traffic; review borderline logs weekly to recalibrate.

demo.code:
parses = [('book restaurant', 0.6), ('book flight', 0.35), ('other', 0.05)]
import math
ent = -sum(p * math.log(p) for _, p in parses)
print(f'ambiguity entropy {ent:.2f} ->', 'CLARIFY' if ent > 0.8 else 'ACT with assumption')

title: Implicit confirmation for low-risk actions
description: For low-stakes actions, the agent states its interpretation and proceeds ('Showing Italian restaurants nearby — say stop if that's wrong') instead of blocking on confirmation. Implicit confirmation keeps flow fast while giving the user a veto; explicit confirmation is reserved for irreversible actions.
method: Classify action risk; low risk -> act with stated interpretation; high risk -> explicit confirm; always allow undo/correction.
usage: Define the risk boundary clearly; err toward explicit confirmation near the boundary.

demo.code:
print('low-risk: showing results for "italian nearby" (say stop if wrong)')
print('high-risk: "Confirm: send $500 refund? [yes/no]"')

title: Domain-scoped intent taxonomies
description: An intent taxonomy (book_restaurant, cancel_booking, modify_booking...) gives the classifier a closed, well-defined label set. Scoped taxonomies beat open-ended guessing: the agent maps requests to known intents with examples per intent, and out-of-scope requests get an honest 'I can't do that' instead of a hallucinated action.
method: Define intents with descriptions and examples; classify into the taxonomy; below-confidence -> out-of-scope handling.
usage: Grow the taxonomy from real unhandled requests; review misclassifications to split or merge intents.

title: Conversation repair strategies
description: When the agent misinterprets, repair strategies recover gracefully: acknowledge the mistake, offer the likely intended options, and remember the correction. Good repair turns errors into training signal — the agent logs the correction to improve future disambiguation.
method: Detect correction signals ('no, I meant...'); apologize briefly; re-parse with the correction; log (misparse, correction) for classifier retraining.
usage: Make corrections cheap (one message); never argue; feed corrections back into training data.

demo.code:
print('agent: booked flight (wrong)')
print('user: no, I meant restaurant')
print('agent: fixed -> restaurant booking; logged misparse for retraining')

title: Personalized disambiguation priors
description: Ambiguity resolves differently per user: 'play something' means jazz for one user, podcasts for another. Personal priors — learned from each user's history — bias parse probabilities so the agent's first guess is usually right for that specific person.
method: Learn per-user parse priors from history; combine with the generic classifier (prior x likelihood); update priors from corrections.
usage: Start with generic priors; personalize gradually; respect privacy — priors stay per-user.

title: Multi-turn reference resolution
description: 'Book it for then' — pronouns and temporal references ('it', 'then', 'there') point at earlier turns. Reference resolution tracks discourse entities across the conversation so follow-ups work naturally without the user repeating everything.
method: Maintain an entity stack per conversation; resolve pronouns/demonstratives to the most recent compatible entity; confirm on low confidence.
usage: Test with real multi-turn logs; confirm resolutions when the entity stack has competing candidates.

demo.code:
entities = ['restaurant Bella', 'friday 7pm']
print('user: "book it for then"')
print('resolved: it =', entities[0], '| then =', entities[1])

title: Proactive option presentation
description: Instead of an open question ('what do you mean?'), the agent presents the top interpretations as tappable options: 'Did you mean: (a) book a restaurant, (b) book a flight?' Options are faster to answer than free text and reveal the agent's understanding for correction.
method: Rank top-k parses; render as options with one-line descriptions; the user's pick fills the intent directly.
usage: Keep options short and distinct; include 'something else' to escape the menu.

demo.code:
options = ['book a restaurant', 'book a flight', 'something else']
print('did you mean:')
for i, o in enumerate(options, 1):
    print(f'  ({i}) {o}')
